purpose: Visual detection of Mobile Bay Jubilee development and biological hypoxia response from waterfront camera imagery.
core_principles: Report only what is visibly supported.
Never infer dissolved oxygen directly from water color or appearance.
A Jubilee may begin offshore before animals reach the beach.
Bottom-dwelling animals appearing at or near the surface are more diagnostic than ordinary pelagic fish activity.
Multiple species responding abnormally is substantially stronger evidence than a single species.
Repeated activity over sequential frames is substantially stronger than an isolated splash.
Absence of visible animals is only negative evidence when detectability and relevant field of view are adequate.
Artificial lights, rain, wakes, insects, glare, debris and normal baitfish activity are important confounders.

shrimp: shrimp visibly popping or flicking at the surface
multiple discrete shrimp-like surface pops or rings
dense shrimp crowding immediately below or at the surface
shrimp concentrated unusually shallow against shoreline, dock or structure
fish_respiratory_stress: fish with mouths repeatedly breaking the surface
groups of fish appearing to gulp at the surface
local behavior sometimes described as smoking
fish holding at the surface rather than swimming normally
fish appearing lethargic, sluggish, disoriented or unusually easy to approach
dense fish compression at shoreline or structure
fish_surface_activity: repeated splashes with biological shape or trajectory
unusual dense fish schooling immediately at the surface
small fish showing widespread surface unrest
crabs: blue crabs swimming at the water surface
crabs making jerky or abnormal movements at the top of the water column
crabs with backs, claws or appendages breaking the surface
crabs climbing stumps, rocks, bulkheads or docks
crabs attempting to leave the water
bottom_fauna: flounder visible away from normal bottom concealment
hogchokers or other flatfish floating or unusually exposed
stingrays unusually shallow or near the surface
eels moving onto sand or shoreline
other normally demersal animals displaced into surface water
spatial_behavior: animals concentrated along a dock, piling line or bulkhead
dense biological band along water edge
offshore surface aggregation of normally bottom-associated animals
surface aggregation extending across more than one part of the frame
birds: dense coordinated feeding over one water area
birds feeding over independently visible fish or shrimp activity
human_response: people using nets, gigs, baskets or buckets
people actively collecting shrimp or crabs
rapid increase in waterfront activity consistent with a reported Jubilee

artificial_light: fish gathered directly under fish lights
weather: rain drops producing repeated surface rings
heavy rain producing apparent boiling surface

montrose_pier_bird: High value for early offshore fish or crab surface aggregation.
High value for bird feeding response.
Do not require shoreline accumulation before treating abnormal offshore bottom-fauna surface activity as meaningful.
montrose_pier_boat: Approximately 200 feet offshore on same pier system.
High value for offshore surface disturbance, fish aggregation, shrimp popping and crab surface activity.
Not spatially independent from Montrose Pier Bird.
pcl_e2_bay_mouth: Faces west toward open Mobile Bay.
Useful for incoming biological aggregation, surface response, birds and transport context.
Less sensitive to animals actually accumulated at the shoreline.
pcl_e2_back_deck: High value for fish holding at surface, shrimp popping, crabs swimming at surface and crabs climbing structure.
Same physical location as E2 Bay Mouth and must not be counted as independent confirmation.
pcl_e3_bay_mouth: Faces west toward Mobile Bay about 50 feet north of E2.
Useful as nearby corroboration but only partially spatially independent.

very_high_value: flounder, eel or stingray displaced abnormally shallow
multiple normally bottom-associated taxa simultaneously at surface
high_value: offshore surface aggregation of crabs or normally bottom-associated fish

strong: multiple independent biological classes show abnormal hypoxia-consistent behavior
clear crustacean or bottom-fauna displacement plus abnormal fish surface behavior
clear repeated abnormal activity corroborated across sequential frames
moderate: one highly diagnostic bottom-fauna signal is clearly visible
multiple shrimp surface pops with adequate visibility and no rain confounder
multiple crabs swimming at surface or climbing structures
clear fish gulping or widespread abnormal surface holding
weak_possible: multiple fish jumps without respiratory-stress behavior
bird feeding without visible biological confirmation
none: no abnormal biological behavior visible when detectability is moderate or high

negative_evidence_rule: No visible activity may reduce visual Jubilee likelihood only when detectability is moderate or high and the camera field of view is capable of observing the relevant biological signal. Poor visibility or an offshore-only field of view must not be treated as evidence that shoreline animals are absent.
temporal_rule: A change across sequential images from normal to increasing surface activity, shrimp popping, fish gulping, crustacean displacement or shoreline concentration is more diagnostic than the same feature in a single frame.
single_frame_warning: Shrimp popping, fish jumping, gulping and animal movement are temporal behaviors. A still frame can miss them. A negative single-frame result should not strongly suppress probability when these behaviors are the target.
